input.question: Why are benzodiazepines (chill pills) so bad for you, but work so well?
input.ground_truth: Benzos really aren't that bad for you, except for the addiction risk. They're particularly safe when compared to what used to be prescribed beforehand, usually barbiturates. (Mixing barbiturates with alcohol is a VERY easy way to die.) You actually have to go well out of your way to manage to OD on benzos. Anyway, as far as benzodiazepines go, Ativan is pretty weak sauce, so if you're only getting occasional scripts for that or Xanax and the scripts don't even have refills on them, you aren't running any real risk of addiction, so I wouldn't worry about that. Why hasn't anyone come up with anything better? Just bad luck. They're always trying; a drug company that could come up with something to treat anxiety that actually *worked* and didn't have any sort of addiction risk would make them literally billions in profits. You may want to check out /r/nootropics too; there's lots of GAD sufferers there always keeping an eye out on the latest research.

Question: Why are benzodiazepines (chill pills) so bad for you, but work so well?

Answer:

response.prediction: Benzodiazepines, often called "chill pills," work very well for quickly reducing anxiety and helping people feel calm because they strongly affect the brain’s calming system. However, they can be bad for you if used for a long time or in high doses because the body can become dependent on them, leading to addiction, withdrawal symptoms, and other health problems. Even though they give fast relief, their side effects and risks increase with long-term use, which is why doctors usually only recommend them for short periods.
